info.bio: La historia de los Cramps empezó en 1972, en la ciudad de Sacramento (California), cuando Lux Interior conoció a Poison Ivy. Los dos se ficharon mutuamente, pero fue dos semanas después cuando descubrieron que ambos se habían apuntado al curso de "Arte y Chamanismo", de la universidad de Sacramento. Pronto surgió el amor y alquilaron un apartamento juntos, donde empezaron a compartir su entusiasmo por el LSD y los sonidos más oscuros del rock & roll de los 50´s.

scenes.name: American Graffiti: revival, garage y power-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: American Graffiti (1973) desata el revival de los cincuenta y sesenta, que suenan más auténticos que el rock corporativo de los setenta: rockabilly, surf, folk-rock, psicodelia, bandas sonoras de terror. Los punks descubren el alma malvada del rockabilly: Suicide inventa el psychobilly y los Cramps el «voodoobilly»; Fleshtones, Raybeats, Stray Cats, Von Lmo. El garage revive con Slickee Boys, Pretenders, Wipers, Real Kids; el power-pop con Cheap Trick, Shoes, Cars, Jonathan Richman y Embarrassment. En California, los Blasters y el cow-punk de Rank And File; Tom Petty como teórico del power-pop, Plimsouls, Redd Kross, Go-Go's, Bangles. El blues para la generación punk: George Thorogood, Fabulous Thunderbirds, J. Geils Band, Dixie Dregs.

podcast.title: Founding Encounter in Sacramento (1972)
podcast.body: In 1972, Cristiuala (later Poison Ivy) met Gilsher (later Lux Interior) while hitchhiking on a road in Sacramento. They discovered a mutual affinity for music, cinema, and spiritual topics, laying the foundation for their future collaboration and intense love story. "1972, una chica llamada Cristiuala se hace autostop en una carretera de sacramento. La recoger y clip por gilser, un estudiante de la misma ciudad."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Meeting and Formation (Sacramento 1972-1975)
podcast.body: Erick perkaiser (Lux interior) and Kristi Marlena Wallace (Poison Ivy) met in Sacramento in 1972. They were drawn together by a shared passion for horror movies and record collecting. By 1975, they had formed The Cramps and began performing at venues like CBGB, sharing stages with bands such as The Ramones, Blondie, Talking Heads, and Patti Smith. "They met in Sacramento back in 1972, and were drawn together by their love of horror movies and record collecting. By 1975, they'd formed the Cramps and were playing places like CBGB alongside their hormones and blondie and talking heads and patty smith and so many others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Couples in Music

podcast.title: Move to "The Cramps" (1973)
podcast.body: In 1973, Cristiuala and Gilsher moved in together to a place they referred to as "The Cramps," or "O Hallo." This predated the official formation of their band but may have served as an early symbolic identifier or shared living space. "En 1973 se fueron a vivir juntos a Crams, o hallo."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: New York Dolls Concert Catalyst (1973)
podcast.body: Attending a New York Dolls concert in 1973 proved to be a life-changing experience for Cristiuala and Gilsher. Following this event, Poison Ivy stated they began to "consume anything that was sexy, wild, and played rock and roll." "Veren con cierto a New York Doll, ese mismo año les cambió la vida."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Move to New York and CBGB Immersion (1975)
podcast.body: In 1975, they relocated to New York, immediately immersing themselves in the burgeoning punk scene centered around the legendary CBGB. They frequented the venue almost nightly, forging connections and friendships with bands like the Ramones and developing an admiration for Suicide. "En 1975 se mudan a New York."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: First Concert at CBGB (1976)
podcast.body: The Cramps performed their first concert in 1976 at CBGB, sharing the stage with the Dead Boys. They quickly became regulars at the venue, frequently appearing on bills with bands like Suicide and Ramones. "Su primer concierto fue en el CBGV junto con los Dead Boys, era 1976."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Bryan Gregory's Mid-Tour Departure (1980)
podcast.body: Shortly after the release of *Songs the Lord Taught Us* in 1980, guitarist Bryan Gregory abandoned the band mid-tour, reportedly taking the band's van and equipment with him. Rumors circulated that he had joined a satanic cult, but the truth was he was experiencing a crisis exacerbated by heroin use. "Poco después de sacar el disco, Reyangre goria abandonó la banda amplia en la gira, llevándose consigo a la forgoneta y el equipo. Corrió el rumor entre las cena y los fans de que se había unido en la secta satanica. Lo cierto es que estaba pasando por una crisis potenciada por la heroína."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Cult Status Before Debut Album (Pre-1980)
podcast.body: The press initially struggled to categorize The Cramps, and they did not release their first album until 1980. This unique situation contributed to their growth into a significant cult phenomenon within the underground music scene. "La prensa a tardón a hacerles caso ya que eran una banda difícil de englobar y nos sacaron disco hasta 1980, cosa que los convirtió en un fenómeno de culto."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Kid Congo Powers' Amicable Departure (Post-1983)
podcast.body: After The Cramps' 1983 album *Smell of Female*, Kid Congo Powers amicably left the band to rejoin his original band, Gun Club. "Poco después, Kid Kongo dejó la banda de forma amistosa, y volvió con Gun Club."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Enduring Core (Until 2006)
podcast.body: While other members of The Cramps changed over time, Lux interior and Poison Ivy remained a constant, together recording and performing until 2006. "Other members of the Cramps came and went, but Lux and Poison Ivy stayed together recording and performing until 2006."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Couples in Music

podcast.title: Lux Interior's Death (February 4, 2009)
podcast.body: Lux interior died suddenly on February 4, 2009, from an aortic dissection, an undiagnosed condition where the body's largest artery ruptures, leading to rapid internal bleeding. He and Poison Ivy had been married for 37 years. "But then on February 4th, 2009, Lux suddenly died after suffering an aortic dissection, an undiagnosed condition where your aorta, the largest artery in your body, bursts, and you bleed out internally in seconds."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Couples in Music

podcast.title: Lux Interior's Death (February 4, 2009)
podcast.body: Lux Interior passed away on February 4, 2009. His death marked the loss of one of rock music's most charismatic frontmen and effectively ended The Cramps. "Luxe Interior murió el 4 de febrero de 2009."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Absence of a Bass Player
podcast.body: In the band's early days, The Cramps did not have a bass player, leaving it entirely up to guitarist Poison Ivy to handle the low-end duties and anchor the music. "Early on, the band didn't have a bass player. It was entirely up to Ivy to hold things down."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Modern Guitar Heroes 2: The Women

podcast.title: Adoption of Stage Names (Poison Ivy Rorschach and Lux Interior)
podcast.body: Cristiuala adopted the stage name Poison Ivy Rorschach, inspired by her passion for comics and psychology. Eric Gilsher chose Lux Interior, a name he found in a car advertisement. These names were part of their effort to shape a 1950s aesthetic filtered through the emerging punk style of New York. "Cristi se bautizó como Poison Ivy Roshach, inspirada por su pasión por los cómics y la psicología. Mientras que Eric se rebautizó como lux interior, un nombre tomado de un anuncio de coches."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Band's End with Lux Interior's Death
podcast.body: The Cramps disbanded after the death of singer Lux Interior in 2009 from an undiagnosed cardiovascular condition. Lux and Poison Ivy had been together for 37 years. "until Lux died of an undiagnosed cardiovascular condition in 2009. Now is the end of the band. Lux and Ivy had been together for 37 years."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Modern Guitar Heroes 2: The Women

podcast.title: Coining the Term "Psychobilly"
podcast.body: The Cramps coined the term "Psychobilly" and used it to promote their concerts on posters and flyers. The term quickly gained traction and became a recognized musical genre. They also employed other descriptive terms for their music, such as "Voodoo Rockabilly" and "Gothabilly." "El término Psycho Bill Lilloy con Yoron para promocionar sus conciertos en carteles y flyers y rápidamente se convirtió en un género musical."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Cult Following
podcast.body: The band developed a strong cult following, frequently performing at CBGB. "They played CBGB a lot and had a cult following until Lux died of an undiagnosed cardiovascular condition in 2009."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Modern Guitar Heroes 2: The Women

podcast.title: Early Sound and Stage Presence
podcast.body: In their early days, The Cramps' musical proposition was clear: a sexy blend of rockabilly and protopunk, even if their technical musicianship had not fully developed. Poison Ivy's lead guitar work was characterized by a unique, raw, and psychedelic sound, complemented by her serious stage attitude. Bryan Gregory contributed a hypnotic rhythm guitar. Early drummer Pam was soon replaced by Miriam Lin, who laid down primitive rhythms. Lux Interior commanded the stage with his spasmodic vocals, described as a "bastard mix between Iggy Pop and an Elvis Presley resurrected from hell." "Por ese entonces no eran tan buenos músicos como Acabrían siendo, pero su propuesta ya estaba clara, una mezcla sexy entre en el Rockabilly y Protopunk."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Famous Monster Sofinland Magazine Logo Source
podcast.body: The Crams (The Cramps) derived their logo from a source found in the magazine "Famous Monster Sofinland." "que sacan un sitio por hacia de la revista Famous Monster Sofinland."

srcs.episode: Cómo los Logos Definieron la Música ｜ Símbolos de Resistencia

podcast.title: Gestating New York Scene
podcast.body: The Cramps are mentioned as one of the bands that were part of the fermenting New York scene in the mid-1970s, contributing to the development of the punk genre. "Suicide, blondie, de gramps, algo se estaba gestando."

srcs.episode: El punk existía antes de Sex Pistols (y era algo salvaje)

podcast.title: Guitar-Oriented Band Played at Chocolate
podcast.body: The Cramps were one of the more "guitar-driven" bands that DJ Tony Vitale "El Gitano" included in his sets at Chocolate. This broader selection, beyond just sinister sounds, also drew in audiences from the punk scene. "Su DJ, Tony Vitale, el jitano, pinchaba bandas siniestras como Bauhaus, Cávered Volter, Othrowingister, con otras más guitarreras como The Crams o The Meteors."

srcs.episode: Cuando Valencia fue la capital mundial del Clubbing

podcast.title: Influence on My Bloody Valentine's Early Sound
podcast.body: The Cramps were noted as an influence on My Bloody Valentine's early recordings, which leaned towards a more garage sound with a production style close to Phil Spector's "wall of sound." "En esas primeras grabaciones podemos ver que tiraban hacia un sonido más garagero, con una producción muy cercana al muro de sonido de espector, ojo a la influencia de The Crams."

srcs.episode: El disco imposible: La historia de Loveless y My Bloody Valentine

podcast.title: Influence on The Black Keys
podcast.body: The Cramps were one of the favorite bands that inspired the short hooks for the songs composed on The Black Keys' *El Camino* album, highlighting their diverse inspirations. "and the Cranps".

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Catching Up With The Black Keys

podcast.title: Lux Interior's Screaming Role
podcast.body: Lux interior, the singer for The Cramps, was later hired specifically for his unique ability to scream. His screaming can be heard in Francis Ford Coppola's film version of "Dracula," attributed to Lux rather than actor Gary Oldman. "In fact, singer Lux interior would later be hired for his ability to scream. If you've ever seen Francis Ford Coppola's version of Dracula, that's not Gary Oldham doing the screaming. That's Lux."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Couples in Music

podcast.title: New York Alternative Scene Presence (1980s)
podcast.body: The Cramps were a significant, though often underrated, band within the New York alternative scene throughout the 1980s. "The Cramps were an important and, in my view, very underrated part of the New York alternative scene throughout the 1980s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Couples in Music

podcast.title: New York City Influence
podcast.body: From New York City, The Cramps were noted for a sound that shared similarities with the harder, more punk rock-influenced American goth acts of the early 1980s. "The same with the cramps from New York City."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 5: Goth

podcast.title: Originators of Psychobilly
podcast.body: The Cramps, originating from New York, were deeply involved in punk and psychobilly, a distinctive bluesy garage rock genre described as sounding like it belongs in a B-movie horror film. Lux and Ivy are credited with "pretty much invented psychobilly." "Hell, Lux and Ivy pretty much invented psychobilly."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Modern Guitar Heroes 2: The Women

podcast.title: Passionate 37-Year Marriage
podcast.body: The relationship between Poison Ivy and Lux Interior was a passionate, reverent, excessive, and creative love that sustained them throughout their shared career, recordings, and "craziness." They were soulmates who became rock and roll legends, having been married for 37 years. "De Krabs fue un amor apasionado y reverente, excesivo y creativo, que los mantuvo juntos en los accionarios, en cada grabación y en cada locura que compartieron. Los almas gemelas que se convirtieron en leyendas del Rock and Roll, llevaban 37 años casados."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Pioneers of Psychobilly
podcast.body: The Cramps, emerging from New York City in the late 70s, were a key band in the Psychobilly genre, a form of punk with a gritty, old-time rockabilly feel and a fascination for horror movies. "If you want to get into that music, try the cramps, who came out of New York City in the late 70s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Post-Punk Explosion Part 7: All the rest

podcast.title: Poison Ivy Rorschach: The Architect of Sound
podcast.body: Poison Ivy was considered the architect of The Cramps' distinctive sound and a "wildest guitar heroine" who redefined how rock and roll was played. She and Lux Interior were the only consistent members from the band's inception until its dissolution. "Fue al arquitectar de su sonido, y una aerobina de la guitarra más salvaje que redefineo la forma en la que se toca el Rock and Roll."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Poison Ivy's Guitar Influence
podcast.body: Poison Ivy's distinctive guitar style was considered a crucial influence on various aspects of the punk rock music scene. "Her guitar style was seen as an essential influence on certain areas of the punk rock universe."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Couples in Music

podcast.title: Poison Ivy's Retirement
podcast.body: Following Lux Interior's death, Poison Ivy, who had turned 70 the previous year, retired to her home in California and largely withdrew from public life, disappearing from the scene. "Con su muerte, el mundo perdió una de los Fronman con más personalidad del Rock, pero no sólo le perdimos a él, junto a Lux, Cristín Terroa de Poison Ivy, y ella, que cumplió 70 años el pasado año, se retiró a su casa de California, donde prácticamente desapareció."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Refusal to Identify with Punk Movement
podcast.body: The Cramps explicitly stated they did not feel identified with the punk movement, arguing that punk "disavowed the origins of rock and roll and wanted to destroy everything." In contrast, The Cramps saw themselves as "mythomaniacs," embracing and reinterpreting rock and roll history. "Ellos decían no sentirse identificados con el movimiento, ya que el punk renego a los orígenes del rock and roll y quería acabar con todo, en cambio de Crams eran unos mitómanos."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Rejection of Mainstream Music (Mid-1970s)
podcast.body: In the mid-1970s, Cristiuala and Gilsher found record stores to be filled with progressive rock and singer-songwriters, which they openly "abhorred." This led them to extensively explore second-hand bins, where they developed a fetish for doo-wop, 60s garage rarities, and especially rockabilly, becoming avid collectors of its obscure B-sides. "En esa época estaban llenas de rock, prodecibo y cantáultores, cosa que aborrecían."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Shared Passions and Early Influences
podcast.body: After their initial meeting, Cristiuala and Gilsher reconnected at an art and shamanism course at the University of Sacramento, after which they remained inseparable. They shared profound passions for the spiritual, the subversive, and the primitive and dark rock and roll of the 1950s, alongside low-budget monster movies, 1950s and 60s science fiction, and Hammer horror films. "Ellos aún no lo saben, pero formarán una de las bandas más influyentes y únicas del punk rock, popularizarán el término psychobili y tendrán una de las historias de amor más intensas de apasionadas de la historia de la música."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Sound and Style
podcast.body: Their distinctive sound was a fusion of garage rock and surf music, leading to the development of genres known as psychobilly and Gotha Billy. The band members were equally influenced by punk and horror movies. "Their sound combined elements of garage rock and surf music and something that became known as psychobilly and Gotha Billy. The Cramps were equal part punks and horror movie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Couples in Music

podcast.title: The Cramps' Definition of Psychobilly vs. Others
podcast.body: When The Cramps toured the United Kingdom, they were surprised to discover other bands identifying with the psychobilly genre. However, The Cramps asserted that their only commonality with these bands was shared references, not their fast and violent musical sound. "Cuando viajaron al reino unido de gira, para su sorpresa, había varias bandas que se englobaban dentro del género, pero ellos defendían que lo único que tenían en común con esas bandas eran las referencias, no compartían su sonido rápido y violento."

srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Visual Aesthetic and Inspirations
podcast.body: The Cramps' visual image was heavily influenced by a 1950s aesthetic, drawing strong inspiration from publications such as *Famous Monsters*, *Shock Theater*, and *Tales from the Crypt*. This vintage horror and sci-fi imagery was then filtered through the punk ethos emerging in New York. "Asi inspiraron fuertemente en publicaciones como Famos Monster, Soft Finland y Tales from the Creed, todo ello pasado por el filtro punk que estaba emergiendo en Nueva York."

xref.title: Andy Fletcher's Cause of Death (2022)
xref.body: Andy Fletcher of Depeche Mode died in 2022 from an aortic dissection, the same undiagnosed condition that caused the death of Lux Interior of The Cramps. "This is the same thing that killed Andy Fletcher of Depeche Mode in 2022."

xref.title: Aortic Dissection Shared by Other Artists
xref.body: Andy Fletcher's cause of death, an aortic dissection, is the same condition that also claimed the lives of actors John Ritter and Alan Thicke, as well as musicians Lux Interior of The Cramps and Peter Steele of Type O Negative. "This is the same thing that killed actors John Ritter and Alan Thick. And it also killed Lux interior singer for the cramps and Peter Steele of the bad typo negative."

xref.title: Cult Status and Influence
xref.body: The Cramps, with Poison Ivy at its core alongside her husband and frontman Lux Interior, became a cult favorite that continues to influence subsequent generations of guitarists, both male and female, as evidenced by bands like Queens of the Stone Age. "And in the process, the Cranps became this weird cult favorite that is still having an impact today. As Queens of the Stone Age, what they think of Ivy."

xref.title: Friends with Blondie and Ramones; Almost Signed to IRS; Influenced B-52s; Background Vocals on Blondie's Autoamerican
xref.body: The B-Girls formed in Toronto in 1977 with a sound closer to British Invasion mid-1960s than hard punk, though their look and attitude were fully punk. They toured with and opened for Teenage Head, the Viletones, and eventually The Clash, then relocated to New York where they became close with Blondie, the Ramones, the Cramps, and the Dead Boys. Members sang background vocals on Blondie's *Autoamerican* (1980), had demos produced by Debbie Harry and Mick Jones of The Clash, and nearly signed with IRS Records — which chose a Los Angeles band called the Go-Go's instead. The Go-Go's were fans of the B-Girls. The B-Girls' existence and sound also influenced a band from Georgia called the B-52s. No album was released before the original lineup fell apart by 1981. "This Canadian punk band influenced not just Blondie and the Go-Go's, but a band visiting New York from Georgia called the B-52s."

xref.title: Musical Style and Contribution to The Cramps
xref.body: Poison Ivy, real name Christie Wallace, was the guitarist and co-writer of all original songs for The Cramps, a New York City-based band known for its unique blend of punk, psychobilly, garage, and horror movie aesthetics. She also occasionally provided vocals and, despite not being a virtuoso, was an inspirational figure in a challenging music scene. "She co-wrote all the groups original songs and occasionally sang."
